sentences.en: Last fall, the BBC made a huge announcement.
sentences.zh: 去年秋天，BBC发布了一个重磅消息。

sentences.en: They had picked a new lead actor for their beloved TV show, Doctor Who.
sentences.zh: 他们为备受喜爱的电视剧《神秘博士》选定了一位新的主演。

sentences.en: Hello, I'm Shuti Gatwa, and I am the next Doctor in the next season of Doctor Who.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是舒提·盖特瓦，我将是下一季《神秘博士》中的下一任博士。

sentences.en: If you need some context, a new lead actor on Doctor Who is like a new Pope being selected, but for nerds.
sentences.zh: 如果你需要背景信息，那么《神秘博士》选出新主演，就相当于选出了一位新教皇，只不过这是针对极客而言的。
那是制片人克里斯·贝鲁比。

sentences.en: This announcement should have been a triumphant moment.
sentences.zh: 这个公告本应是一个值得庆祝的时刻。

sentences.en: After all, the actor Shuti Gatwa was the first Black performer cast as the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，演员舒提·盖特瓦是第一位被选为“博士”的黑人表演者。

sentences.en: But when this video came out, the announcement was quickly overshadowed by something that should have been totally mundane.
sentences.zh: 但当这段视频发布时，这个公告很快就被一件本该完全平凡的事情给掩盖了。

sentences.en: Gatwa's first name is spelled N-C-U-T-I.
But the closed captions on YouTube replaced his name with a swear word.
sentences.zh: 但YouTube上的隐藏式字幕却把他的名字替换成了一个脏话。
大家好，我是舒提·盖特瓦。

sentences.en: The captions auto-corrected his name to,
sentences.zh: 字幕却自动纠正他的名字为：
大家好，我是舒提·盖特沃斯。

sentences.en: But it was far from an isolated incident.
When you start looking for closed caption failures, you see them pretty much everywhere.
sentences.zh: 当你开始关注隐藏式字幕的故障时，你会发现它们几乎无处不在。

sentences.en: I turned on closed captions for a week on broadcast TV, YouTube, pretty much anywhere I was watching stuff.
sentences.zh: 我试着在广播电视、YouTube以及我观看内容的几乎任何地方开启了一周的隐藏式字幕。

sentences.en: And I noticed so many errors.
sentences.zh: 我注意到了太多的错误。

sentences.en: The fictional country in Black Panther, Wakanda, it became War, Canada.
sentences.zh: 《黑豹》中的虚构国家瓦坎达，变成了“战争，加拿大”。

sentences.en: Bill Murray and Dan Aykroyd were suddenly part of an elite group called the Ghost Buses.
sentences.zh: 比尔·默瑞和丹·艾克罗伊德突然成了名为“幽灵巴士”的精英小组成员。

sentences.en: There's actually an academic high-minded term to describe this phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 实际上，有一个学术性且高大上的术语来描述这种现象。

sentences.en: Craptions are captions that are crappy.
sentences.zh: “烂字幕”（Craptions）就是指那些糟糕透顶的字幕。

sentences.en: She wrote about craptions for The Atlantic magazine.
sentences.zh: 她曾为《大西洋》杂志撰写过关于“烂字幕”的文章。

sentences.en: And she says there are many, many ways a caption can be crappy.
sentences.zh: 她说，字幕变烂的方式有很多很多种。

sentences.en: So it's just sort of one long run-on sentence.
sentences.zh: 所以它看起来就像是一个冗长的长难句。

sentences.en: So they are sort of halfway there, captions.
sentences.zh: 所以它们只能算是半吊子的字幕。

sentences.en: Look, bad closed captions can be really funny.
sentences.zh: 听着，糟糕的隐藏式字幕确实可能很好笑。

sentences.en: But captions are a critical tool for lots and lots of people.
sentences.zh: 但字幕对于很多人来说是一个至关重要的工具。

sentences.en: There's people learning a new language.
sentences.zh: 有正在学习新语言的人。

sentences.en: People like me, who for the life of me cannot understand the Irish accents on Derry Girls.
sentences.zh: 像我这样的人，无论如何都听不懂《德里女孩》里爱尔兰口音的人。

sentences.en: And of course, captions are essential for people who are deaf and hard of hearing.
sentences.zh: 当然，字幕对于失聪和听力障碍人士来说是必不可少的。

sentences.en: In the United States, that's about 15% of the adult population.
sentences.zh: 在美国，这大约占成年人口的15%。

sentences.en: And with so many craptions out there, those folks are often left trying to piece together meaning from some bizarre sentences or to just stop watching.
sentences.zh: 由于市面上充斥着这么多“烂字幕”，这些人往往只能试图从一些离奇的句子中拼凑出含义，或者干脆放弃观看。

sentences.en: The issue of crappy captions isn't a new thing.
sentences.zh: 糟糕字幕的问题并不是什么新鲜事。

sentences.en: Activists have been fighting for accurate, widespread closed captioning for decades.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，活动家们一直在为准确、广泛的隐藏式字幕而斗争。

sentences.en: And it's not clear when, if ever, they will become a reality.
sentences.zh: 而且目前还不清楚它们何时（如果真能实现的话）才能成为现实。
糟糕的字幕不仅仅是令人讨厌。

sentences.en: They're supposed to be illegal, at least for television.
sentences.zh: 它们本应是非法的，至少在电视上是这样。

sentences.en: In America, the FCC is responsible for making sure the airwaves are accessible for everybody.
sentences.zh: 在美国，联邦通信委员会（FCC）负责确保广播电视对所有人都是无障碍的。

sentences.en: And since 1996, they've required all TV shows to include captions that are, quote,
sentences.zh: 自1996年以来，他们要求所有电视节目必须包含字幕，且必须是，引用原文：

sentences.en: accurate, synchronous, complete, and properly placed.
sentences.zh: 准确、同步、完整且位置得当的。

sentences.en: Broadcasters in the United States also have to comply with guidelines under the Americans with Disabilities Act, which was passed in 1990.
sentences.zh: 美国的广播公司还必须遵守1990年通过的《美国残疾人法案》（ADA）下的指导方针。

sentences.en: The ADA says all businesses that serve the public or places of public accommodation must be equally available to everyone,
sentences.zh: ADA规定，所有服务公众的企业或公共场所必须对每个人平等开放，

sentences.en: which means broadcast TV needs to be accessible for the deaf and hard of hearing.
sentences.zh: 这意味着广播电视必须对失聪和听力障碍人士无障碍。

sentences.en: Taken together, the FCC and ADA rules were pretty clear.
sentences.zh: 综上所述，FCC和ADA的规则非常明确。

sentences.en: For TV, you need to caption.
sentences.zh: 对于电视，你需要提供字幕。

sentences.en: And you need to caption well.
sentences.zh: 而且你需要提供高质量的字幕。

sentences.en: And for a while, those rules were enough.
sentences.zh: 有一段时间，这些规则是足够的。

sentences.en: Until the rise of streaming TV.
sentences.zh: 直到流媒体电视的兴起。

sentences.en: Howard Rosenblum is the CEO of the National Association of the Deaf, or the NAD.
sentences.zh: 霍华德·罗森布鲁姆是美国全国聋人协会（NAD）的首席执行官。

sentences.en: Howard himself is deaf, and we interviewed him over Zoom with the assistance of an ASL interpreter.
sentences.zh: 霍华德本人是聋人，我们在美国手语（ASL）翻译的协助下通过Zoom采访了他。

sentences.en: Throughout this story, you'll hear her voice representing his answers.
sentences.zh: 在整个故事中，你将听到她的声音来传达他的回答。

sentences.en: Howard points to 2007 as the first time the NAD got involved in captions for streaming, when Netflix launched its on-demand service.
sentences.zh: 霍华德指出，2007年是NAD首次介入流媒体字幕问题的时间，当时Netflix推出了点播服务。

sentences.en: At the time, if you recall, it was the era of DVDs in the postal mail, right?
sentences.zh: 当时，如果你还记得的话，那还是邮寄DVD的时代，对吧？

sentences.en: Ironically, there was no law which required DVDs to be captioned.
sentences.zh: 讽刺的是，当时并没有法律要求DVD必须配有字幕。

sentences.en: But I would say roughly 85% to 90% of them were.
sentences.zh: 但我可以说，大约85%到90%的DVD都有字幕。

sentences.en: So many of the members of NAD were Netflix subscribers.
sentences.zh: 所以NAD的许多成员都是Netflix的用户。

sentences.en: We'd get our DVDs in the postal mail, and it was all good.
sentences.zh: 我们通过邮寄收到DVD，一切都很顺利。

sentences.en: Netflix decided then to pivot to streaming.
However, streaming at the time, there was almost none.
sentences.zh: 然而，当时的流媒体几乎没有字幕。
可能只有10%的内容有字幕。

sentences.en: Howard and the NAD approached Netflix about this issue.
sentences.zh: 霍华德和NAD就这个问题接触了Netflix。

sentences.en: But at the time, Netflix argued the rules didn't apply to them.
sentences.zh: 但当时，Netflix辩称这些规则不适用于他们。

sentences.en: They weren't television, so they weren't under the jurisdiction of the FCC.
sentences.zh: 他们不是电视台，所以不受FCC管辖。

sentences.en: And Netflix argued the ADA didn't apply to them either.
sentences.zh: 而且Netflix还辩称ADA也不适用于他们。
再次请出作家琳达·贝斯纳。

sentences.en: Title III of the ADA says that in places of public accommodation, deaf and hard-of-hearing people must be accommodated.
sentences.zh: ADA的第三章规定，在公共场所，必须为失聪和听力障碍人士提供便利。

sentences.en: So they should have an experience equal to that of a person who is not deaf or hard-of-hearing.
sentences.zh: 所以他们应该获得与非失聪或听力正常的人同等的体验。

sentences.en: Netflix's argument was, we're not subject to the ADA because we're not a place.
sentences.zh: Netflix的论点是，我们不受ADA约束，因为我们不是一个“场所”。

sentences.en: They were like, well, we're not an amusement park or, like, you know, some kind of public forum.
sentences.zh: 他们就像是说，好吧，我们又不是游乐园，或者你知道的，某种公共论坛。

sentences.en: We're not a physical location, so we don't have to do this.
sentences.zh: 我们不是实体地点，所以我们不必这样做。

sentences.en: The National Association of the Deaf argued that, okay, sure, Netflix is not a physical place, but isn't it kind of a social place?
sentences.zh: 美国全国聋人协会反驳说，好吧，当然，Netflix不是一个实体场所，但它难道不是一种社交场所吗？

sentences.en: You know, what about a family watching a Netflix show together?
sentences.zh: 你知道，一家人一起看Netflix节目又怎么说？

sentences.en: Like, this is a social experience.
Why should there be a member of that family who is excluded from that content?
sentences.zh: 为什么家庭中会有成员被排除在内容之外呢？

sentences.en: In 2011, the NAD sued Netflix in a Massachusetts court.
sentences.zh: 2011年，NAD在马萨诸塞州法院起诉了Netflix。

sentences.en: The judge agreed that the ADA applies to Netflix and issued a consent decree,
sentences.zh: 法官同意ADA适用于Netflix，并发布了一项同意令，

sentences.en: saying Netflix had to provide captions for all of its streaming content within four years.
sentences.zh: 要求Netflix在四年内为其所有流媒体内容提供字幕。

sentences.en: Today, the full Netflix library is captioned.
sentences.zh: 今天，Netflix的整个库都有字幕了。

sentences.en: They have teams of captioners working on every show,
sentences.zh: 他们有专门的字幕制作团队为每个节目工作，

sentences.en: and some of their captions are really good, and some of them are only okay.
sentences.zh: 有些字幕做得非常好，有些则只能说是还行。

sentences.en: But according to Howard Rosenblum of the NAD, Netflix has done a fairly good job.
sentences.zh: 但据NAD的霍华德·罗森布鲁姆说，Netflix做得相当不错。

sentences.en: Once that case was done and dusted, we began to approach other companies like Hulu, Amazon.
sentences.zh: 一旦那个案子尘埃落定，我们就开始接触其他公司，比如Hulu、亚马逊。

sentences.en: So all three of them agreed to the terms of a phased-in captioning approach.
sentences.zh: 最终，这三家公司都同意了分阶段实施字幕方案的条款。

sentences.en: Since the Netflix case, the National Association of the Deaf has been playing a game of whack-a-mole with the internet.
sentences.zh: 自Netflix案以来，美国全国聋人协会一直在互联网上玩“打地鼠”游戏。

sentences.en: Basically, a new streaming thing will crop up,
sentences.zh: 基本上，一个新的流媒体平台出现，

sentences.en: and the NAD will helpfully remind them about their legal requirements to caption stuff.
sentences.zh: NAD就会贴心地提醒他们关于提供字幕的法律要求。

sentences.en: The NAD has worked with companies like Zoom and Microsoft Teams to encourage live captions for online meetings.
sentences.zh: NAD曾与Zoom和Microsoft Teams等公司合作，鼓励为在线会议提供实时字幕。

sentences.en: And in 2015, the NAD sued Harvard and MIT for not providing captions for their online courses.
sentences.zh: 2015年，NAD起诉了哈佛大学和麻省理工学院，因为他们没有为在线课程提供字幕。

sentences.en: Most recently, the NAD sued SiriusXM for not providing transcripts on their podcasts.
sentences.zh: 最近，NAD起诉了SiriusXM，因为他们的播客没有提供文字记录。

sentences.en: Nearly all podcasts are recorded, right?
sentences.zh: 几乎所有的播客都是录制好的，对吧？

sentences.en: There's no excuse for not providing a transcript.
sentences.zh: 没有理由不提供文字记录。

sentences.en: Full disclosure here, 99PI is owned by SiriusXM,
but I'll note that our show does provide transcripts to all of our episodes.
sentences.zh: 但我得指出，我们的节目确实为所有剧集提供了文字记录。

sentences.en: While there's been a lot of progress on the issue of streaming captions,
sentences.zh: 虽然在流媒体字幕问题上已经取得了很大进展，

sentences.en: there's one internet goliath the NAD won't go after.
sentences.zh: 但有一个互联网巨头是NAD不会去碰的。

sentences.en: It's actually a place used by 80% of Americans,
sentences.zh: 它实际上是一个被80%的美国人使用的平台，

sentences.en: where people watch billions of hours of content every day.
sentences.zh: 人们每天在那里观看数十亿小时的内容。

sentences.en: Linda Besner spoke to YouTube about this problem a couple of years ago,
sentences.zh: 琳达·贝斯纳几年前曾就这个问题与YouTube沟通过，

sentences.en: And back then, they made it clear they had no plans to require captions for all of their videos.
sentences.zh: 当时他们明确表示，没有计划要求所有视频都必须配有字幕。

sentences.en: They did say, for example, for things like sort of live citizen journalism,
sentences.zh: 他们确实说过，例如，对于像某种实时公民新闻之类的东西，

sentences.en: like the spokesperson I spoke with gave the example of Arab Spring.
sentences.zh: 我采访的发言人举了“阿拉伯之春”的例子。

sentences.en: You know, if it's somebody who is, you know,
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果有人，你知道，

sentences.en: posting video of some event that is occurring around them,
sentences.zh: 正在发布他们周围发生的某个事件的视频，

sentences.en: are you really going to flag for removal that video because it doesn't have transcriptions?
sentences.zh: 你真的会因为该视频没有文字记录就标记并删除它吗？

sentences.en: Even though YouTube isn't legally required to provide closed captions,
sentences.zh: 尽管YouTube在法律上不需要提供隐藏式字幕，

sentences.en: they have a lot of deaf and hard of hearing users.
sentences.zh: 但他们有很多失聪和听力障碍的用户。

sentences.en: In 2009, YouTube tried addressing the problem of closed captions
sentences.zh: 2009年，YouTube试图通过为部分视频推出人工智能生成的字幕来解决这个问题。

sentences.en: by rolling out AI-generated captions for some of their videos.
It hasn't been a smooth ride.
sentences.zh: 自动字幕是使用谷歌的通用语音模型创建的，

sentences.en: The automatic captions are created with Google's universal speech model,
sentences.zh: 该模型使用语音识别技术和人工智能来识别单词，

sentences.en: which uses speech recognition technology and AI to identify words
sentences.zh: 然后将它们组合成连贯的句子。

sentences.en: and then put them together into coherent sentences.
sentences.zh: 预测性文本是某种，你知道的，

sentences.en: Predictive text is something that, you know,
sentences.zh: 你可能从手机上的自动更正功能中熟悉的东西，

sentences.en: you may be familiar with from autocorrect on your phone,
sentences.zh: 就像你刚开始写一个句子，它就想帮你填空一样，

sentences.en: that it's like you started a sentence and then it wants to fill in your blank,
sentences.zh: 很像你母亲可能会做的那样。

sentences.en: much like maybe your mother does.
sentences.zh: 而且很像你母亲，有时他们根本不知道你要说什么。

sentences.en: And much like your mother, sometimes they don't know what you are going to say.
sentences.zh: 你不得不说，妈，不是那样的，我不是，

sentences.en: And you have to be like, mom, that's not like I'm not,
sentences.zh: 我其实是想表达相反的观点。

sentences.en: I'm actually trying to make the opposite point right now.
sentences.zh: 自动字幕的早期阶段相当粗糙，

sentences.en: The early days of automatic captions were pretty rough,
sentences.zh: 瑞奇·波因特对此记忆犹新。

sentences.en: and Rikki Pointer remembers them well.
sentences.zh: 瑞奇是一位失聪的YouTube博主，在2009年，

sentences.en: Rikki is a deaf YouTuber, and in 2009,
sentences.zh: 她当时正在使用全新的自动字幕观看大量的美容视频。

sentences.en: she was watching a lot of beauty videos using the brand new automatic captions.
sentences.zh: 我记得我当时在看一个关于遮瑕膏的视频，

sentences.en: I remember I was watching a video about concealers
and the automatic captions I had them on,
sentences.zh: 它们竟然把“遮瑕膏”这个词说成了“斑马”，那种哺乳动物，那种动物，不管是什么，

sentences.en: and they were saying zebra, the mammal, the animal, whatever,
in place of the word concealers, which was so bizarre.
sentences.zh: 瑞奇开始她的YouTube生涯时是制作关于化妆和美容产品的视频，

sentences.en: Rikki started her YouTube career making videos about makeup and beauty products,
sentences.zh: 但她想做点不同的事情。

sentences.en: but she wanted to do something different.
sentences.zh: 所以在2014年，瑞奇制作了一个视频，标题为

sentences.en: So in 2014, Rikki produced a video called
sentences.zh: 《你不该对失聪或听力障碍人士说的话》，

sentences.en: Things You Shouldn't Say to People Who Are Deaf or Hard of Hearing,
sentences.zh: 她在视频中讽刺了那些听力正常的人总是问她的无知问题。

sentences.en: where she lampoons the clueless questions she was always being asked by hearing folks.
I don't know, but come over here, I'll cough on you,
sentences.zh: 我不知道，但你过来，我对着你咳嗽，

sentences.en: Why don't you know sign language?
You must not really be deaf.
deafness has to do with whether or not your ears work
sentences.zh: 耳聋与你的耳朵是否正常工作有关，

sentences.en: and not the languages that you know.
sentences.zh: 而与你懂不懂某种语言无关。

sentences.en: A couple of Rikki's videos focused on the issue of closed captioning,
sentences.zh: Rikki 的几期视频聚焦于隐藏字幕的问题，

sentences.en: and in one video, Rikki made a call to ARMS,
sentences.zh: 在其中一期视频里，Rikki 给 ARMS 打了电话，

sentences.en: asking her fellow YouTubers to ditch automatic captions
sentences.zh: 呼吁她的 YouTuber 同行们弃用自动字幕，

sentences.en: and write their own captions instead,
or better yet, to hire a professional service to make the captions for them.
sentences.zh: 或者更好的是，聘请专业服务来为他们制作字幕。

sentences.en: The campaign for human closed captions went viral,
sentences.zh: 这场关于人工隐藏字幕的运动迅速走红，

sentences.en: and Rikki caught the attention of some of YouTube's biggest stars.
sentences.zh: Rikki 也引起了 YouTube 一些大牌明星的注意。

sentences.en: I want to make my little community here on YouTube more inclusive,
sentences.zh: 我想让我在 YouTube 上的这个小社区更具包容性，

sentences.en: and one of the ways that I have decided to do that in the new year
sentences.zh: 我决定在新的一年里实现这一目标的方法之一，

sentences.en: is by closed captioning every single one of my videos.
sentences.zh: 就是为我的每一期视频都加上隐藏字幕。

sentences.en: Yeah, Tyler Oakley made a video while I was on a plane on the way to LA, actually,
sentences.zh: 没错，其实 Tyler Oakley 在我飞往洛杉矶的飞机上就做了一期视频，

sentences.en: and it was like titled Hear Me Out or something,
sentences.zh: 标题好像叫《听我说》之类的，

sentences.en: and I was in the thumbnail,
and he was talking about the importance of captions,
sentences.zh: 他在视频里谈到了字幕的重要性，

sentences.en: and I had no idea until I had landed in LA,
and I was getting so many notifications.
sentences.zh: 才发现收到了海量的通知，对此一无所知。

sentences.en: ...and tried to encourage me to do it.
I saw a video from a YouTuber named Rikki Pointer
sentences.zh: 我看到了一个名叫 Rikki Pointer 的 YouTuber 发布的视频，
